transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Acme Head of Search), Samir Khan (Acme Staff ML Eng), Priya Desai (Acme CTO)

Summary: Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for Acme's site search use case. Walkthrough of Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint, vector store integration patterns, and the reranking endpoint/approach from hosted API + Console Optimize suggestions. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, data residency and SOC2/KMS questions. Agreed next steps: send pricing, run 1-week trial with customer sample queries, share reranker notebook.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint, embedding dims / models, batching & latency, Console demo (routes + Optimize suggestions), security (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), trial benchmarks and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jordan Reyes: Good, thanks. Excited to see the demo. We're trying to improve relevance for product search, right now the results are kinda all over, especially long tail queries.
[00:14] Ethan Liu: Great. Quick agenda — we'll show hosted embeddings, how you'd plug them into your vector store, then the hosted reranker endpoint which we use to rerank top-K results, and finally a quick peek at Console Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization.
[00:24] Samir Khan: Sounds good. We use Elasticsearch as primary index + Pinecone for vectors for some experiments. We want to reduce latency and cost while improving click-through on long-tail queries.
[00:33] Maya Patel: Perfect, that lines up with a lot we've seen. Question — is data residency a constraint, or is hosted acceptable?
[00:40] Jordan Reyes: Hosted is fine for now but we need SOC 2 and encryption in transit, plus KMS support for keys. Also SSO integration is a must.
[00:48] Maya Patel: Yep all supported; we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, and KMS integrations — we'll send those docs after.
[00:55] Ethan Liu: Alright jumping in — I'm sharing my screen. (screen share) Here is the hosted embeddings endpoint, you hit /v1/embeddings with model=id, input=text. We demo with redwood-embed-large as an example.
[01:10] Ethan Liu: Quick note on dims — 1536 vs 1024 options, and we profile for latency. For Acme's traffic shape, if most queries are short, 1024-dim faster and cheaper; for semantic precision on long tail, 1536 helps.
[01:26] Jordan Reyes: Can you quantify the latency difference? We care about 95th percentile under 200ms.
[01:32] Ethan Liu: Sure — on our hosted API region in us-west, 1024 models for single request median ~40ms, p95 around 110-140ms depending on batching; 1536 median ~60-80ms, p95 150-220ms. With continuous batching you can reduce cost but p95 will trade off a bit. We'll include detailed perf profiles in the follow-up.
[01:50] Samir Khan: When you say batching, are you referring to client side batching or Redwood continuous batching? We have bursty traffic.
[01:56] Ethan Liu: Both. Client-side batching reduces round trips; Redwood also has automatic continuous batching on the serving runtime where we coalesce requests for improved GPU utilization. You can set a latency SLO and batching aggressiveness. For Acme, we recommend conservative batching to keep p95 under 200ms.
[02:10] Priya Desai: Any guidance on vector store — we'd rather not rip out ES. We want to keep ECM search and add vector reranking on top.
[02:18] Ethan Liu: That's a common pattern. Use your existing ES for lexical recall, request top-K (say 50), then call Redwood embeddings or stored embeddings and use our reranker endpoint to score and return reordered results. Reranker reduces the amount of vectors you need to score in the LLM path.
[02:30] Jordan Reyes: Walk me through reranker pricing and where it runs — is it hosted or do we need dedicated?
[02:36] Maya Patel: Hosted runs on our multitenant infra; you pay per rerank call (per-query) and tokens for any model generation. Dedicated capacity is an option if you want lower p95 SLAs or data isolation; pricing differs. We'll send both options.
[02:50] Ethan Liu: Demo time — here's a simple pipeline: user query -> ES top50 -> embeddings for query -> call /v1/rerank with candidate texts + query embedding -> rerank returns scores. I'm uploading a sample request in the Console.
[03:05] Ethan Liu: (shows Console) Console shows per-route metrics, token breakdown, and Optimize suggestions. For this dataset Optimize suggests lowering embedding dim for high QPS slices and enabling prefix KV cache for common query prefixes.
[03:20] Jordan Reyes: That Console Optimize suggestion — how does it generate recommendations? Based on traffic patterns and P99 latency targets?
[03:26] Ethan Liu: Exactly — it pulls request histograms, model perf profiles, and suggests batching window, quantization profile if you self-host, or model variant on hosted to meet cost/latency goals.
[03:36] Samir Khan: Any examples where reranker materially moved CTR? Curious numbers.
[03:40] Maya Patel: Yes — for a retail customer we saw +12% CTR and 18% reduction in perceived unsuccessful sessions after tuning the reranker and adjusting recall threshold. Results vary but that's the sort of impact.
[03:52] Jordan Reyes: Ok show me a real rerank request/response.
[03:55] Ethan Liu: Here — sample request, you pass candidates as an array with metadata, set max_candidates, and the reranker returns scores and optional explain tokens. Example payload in the chat. (reads) The response is a list of indices sorted by score. Note, transcripts sometimes show minor differences in param names, but api is stable.
[04:15] Samir Khan: Does the reranker keep any customer text? What's retention?
[04:19] Maya Patel: By default hosted API is transient, we don't persist user data for training. For enterprise contracts we can sign custom retention. We'll include our data retention policy and the SOC2 docs.
[04:28] Priya Desai: KMS — can we bring our key?
[04:31] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments and dedicated can support bring-your-own-key integrations with HSMs. Hosted supports envelope encryption with KMS integrations — details in the docs we'll share.
[04:45] Jordan Reyes: Good. On integration complexity — how fast could we get a POC running? 1-2 engineers?
[04:49] Ethan Liu: Typically 1-2 engineers can wire a flow in a week if you have query logs. We'll run a bench: you provide 5k sample queries + labels, we'll run a week-long hosted trial and produce p95/p50 latency and relevance lift numbers.
[05:02] Jordan Reyes: OK we'll try for that.
[05:05] Ethan Liu: Now live example — I'm going to run a couple of queries against a sample corpus. (executes) Query: "waterproof hiking jacket womens large" returns top-K from ES first, then reranker reorders based on semantic match. You can see the score delta.
[05:20] Jordan Reyes: The re-ranked top result looks more relevant, I see titles with exact size/color. How much extra latency from the rerank call?
[05:25] Ethan Liu: Typically adding reranker for top-50 adds ~30-80ms depending on model and payload size; for top-10 it's much less. You can trade recall size for latency.
[05:34] Samir Khan: For us top-20 might be sweet spot.
[05:36] Ethan Liu: Makes sense. Also note you can cache embeddings for items (document vectors) and only compute query embeddings at runtime — that saves cost. Our SDKs show common caching patterns.
[05:46] Jordan Reyes: About cost — what's ballpark for 1M queries a month with top-20 rerank?
[05:49] Maya Patel: We'll send a modeled estimate — rough numbers: embeddings at X per 1k, reranker at Y per 1k, plus data transfer. We typically prepare a few commit tiers with expected unit economics.
[05:59] Priya Desai: Can we run A/B tests and measure lift in Console?
[06:02] Ethan Liu: Yes — Console supports rollout policies, canary, A/B and ties to metrics like CTR and search success. You can instrument events and our dashboard will show per-route impact.
[06:12] Jordan Reyes: Any gotchas around HTML or noise in catalog text?
[06:15] Ethan Liu: Preprocessing matters — strip HTML, normalize SKU tokens. Also annotate signals like click history as features for reranker if available. Our reranker accepts optional structured features. We'll provide best practices doc.
[06:27] Samir Khan: Quick question on developer ergonomics — SDKs for Node and Python?
[06:30] Maya Patel: Yes Node and Python SDKs, plus REST curl. We'll share sample repo.
[06:35] (brief pause while Ethan pulls up sample repo)
[06:47] Jordan Reyes: On compliance, we need SOC2 plus contract clause for encryption at rest.
[06:52] Maya Patel: Understood — we'll attach SOC2 report and the encryption/KMS spec. For dedicated/private we can support more stringent language.
[07:00] Samir Khan: Can we run a small benchmark now? Maybe run 50 queries from our sample quickly? We don't have the sample in call though.
[07:06] Ethan Liu: If you can drop the file in the shared folder after the call, we can run the benchmark and share results within 48 hours.
[07:13] Jordan Reyes: Will do.
[07:15] Ethan Liu: Ok jumping to Console Optimize — here's a recommendations tab which flagged that for high-frequency SKU lookups we should enable prefix caching and reduce embedding dim for those slices. It also recommended using reranker only for long-tail queries via routing policy to reduce cost.
[07:30] Jordan Reyes: Routing policy — can we route by intent or by route?
[07:33] Ethan Liu: You can route by route, region, or a small custom policy (e.g., queries that match a regex or low-doc-count categories). We can set automatic fallback to lexical-only on heavy load.
[07:44] Priya Desai: For the trial what metrics should we track as success?
[07:47] Maya Patel: Typical success metrics: +CTR on organic search, decreased time-to-first-click, lower unsuccessful searches, and p95 latency under your target. We'll help define the eval set.
[07:58] Jordan Reyes: Sounds good.
[08:00] (wrap up discussion, timeline and next steps)
[08:04] Maya Patel: Quick recap — we'll send: pricing + dedicated options, SOC2 and KMS docs, reranker notebook, and a sample bench plan. Ethan will run a bench once you upload 5k queries and labels. We'll plan follow-up deep dive week of Nov 14. Any other questions?
[08:18] Priya Desai: That's all from me.
[08:21] Jordan Reyes: Nothing else. Thanks.
[08:23] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone.
[08:25] (call ends)
